To prepare a corpus for a reliable NovaLearn deployment, the customer should follow the Phase 2 corpus preparation process, which requires close collaboration with content owners and typically takes 1 week [NL-005#NL-005-S04]. The customer must:

- **Audit document sources**: Identify where company knowledge is stored (SharePoint, Google Drive, local servers, Confluence), catalog file formats, and document the volume of files in each repository [NL-005#NL-005-S04].
- **Inspect formats**: Ensure all documents are in supported formats (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, HTML, Markdown, CSV, XLSX); flag legacy or unsupported file types for conversion [NL-005#NL-005-S04].
- **Identify OCR needs**: Scan the corpus for image-only or scanned PDFs. These lack native text layers and must be flagged for OCR processing because they require OCR for reliable citations and may extend the onboarding timeline [NL-005#NL-005-S04].
- **Define document taxonomy**: Design the tagging system in KnowledgeHub (e.g., department, product, region) and set up custom metadata schemas to enable precise filtering and retrieval [NL-005#NL-005-S04].

Before delivering the Corpus Inventory Sheet, content owners must verify the following checklist [NL-005#NL-005-S04]:
- All file names are descriptive and exclude special symbols.
- No duplicate copies of policy manuals exist in the inventory.
- Scanned files are separated and marked "OCR Required: True".
- Every document has an assigned department and owner.
- Source files contain clear heading structures (H1, H2, H3).

These checks ensure the corpus is optimized for retrieval and supports reliable, citation-backed answers [NL-005#NL-005-S01].
